record.paper_title: Variants of the focusing NLS equation. Derivation, justification and open problems related to filamentation
record.original_question:
For the hyperbolic or non-elliptic cubic NLS

 i partial_t v + (Delta_perp - partial_z^2)v + |v|^2 v = 0

in dimensions 2 and 3, can one prove that every H^1 solution is global, despite the lack of the standard elliptic structure of the usual focusing cubic NLS?

evidence.quote: Thus an interesting problem would be to prove that the cubic NLS equation (69) (i.e. in the case of normal GVD) does not have finite time blow up solutions, whether this is due to pulse splitting, or to some other phenomenon.
Open Problem 6. Prove that the solutions to equation (69) are global in dimension 2 and 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the hyperbolic (non-elliptic) cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
\[
 i\,\partial_t v + (\Delta_\perp - \partial_z^2)\,v + |v|^2 v = 0,
\]
posed on $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d\in\{2,3\}$, where the spatial coordinate is split as $(x_\perp,z)$ with $x_\perp\in\mathbb{R}^{d-1}$ and $z\in\mathbb{R}$, and where $\Delta_\perp$ denotes the Laplacian in the transverse variables $x_\perp$. Equivalently, the spatial operator is the indefinite (Lorentzian-type) operator $\sum_{j=1}^{d-1}\partial_{x_j}^2 - \partial_z^2$ in place of the standard Laplacian. Initial data $v(0,\cdot)=v_0$ are taken in the Sobolev space $H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$.

Prove or disprove: every solution $v\in C([0,T_{\max});H^1(\mathbb{R}^d))$ extends globally in time, i.e.\ $T_{\max}=+\infty$, despite the absence of the elliptic (positive-definite) structure of the standard focusing cubic NLS and the loss of coercivity of the conserved energy that this entails. In particular, rule out (or exhibit) finite-time blow-up phenomena such as pulse-splitting in dimensions $d=2$ and $d=3$.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches on hyperbolic/non-elliptic cubic NLS turn up results on special solutions (radial standing and self-similar waves in 2D), nonexistence of localized travelling waves, and related modulational analysis, but no proof of global $H^1$ existence in dimensions 2 or 3 nor a finite-time blow-up construction. The global existence question for the non-elliptic cubic NLS in dimensions 2 and 3 thus appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Radial standing and self-similar waves for the hyperbolic cubic NLS in 2D
status_evidence.snippet: Studies special radial standing and self-similar wave solutions of the hyperbolic cubic NLS in 2D, indicating ongoing investigation rather than a settled global existence theory.
status_evidence.claim: Research on the 2D hyperbolic cubic NLS focuses on special solutions, with the global $H^1$ theory not yet established.

status_evidence.title: Some special solutions to the Hyperbolic NLS equation
status_evidence.snippet: The hyperbolic operator changes substantially the nonlinear wave interaction; in one direction it is focusing, in the orthogonal one defocusing.
status_evidence.claim: The mixed focusing/defocusing character of the non-elliptic cubic NLS distinguishes it from the standard focusing NLS and complicates global existence analysis.

status_evidence.title: On the hyperbolic nonlinear Schrödinger equations
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work on hyperbolic NLS continues to address well-posedness aspects of the model.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research on hyperbolic NLS suggests global existence in $H^1$ for the cubic case in 2D/3D has not been fully resolved.
